common_name: Regina's Disco Lounge Crinum Lily (Fragrant Pink-Striped Rescue Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant the large bulb with its neck at or just above soil level in fertile, evenly moist soil in a sunny to lightly shaded bed. This is an especially vigorous C. bulbispermum x C. zeylanicum hybrid, so give it plenty of room to bulk up into a multi-bulb clump.

directions: This heirloom crinum was rescued from a Carolina nightclub parking lot by plantsman Jenks Farmer, and it retains the toughness of a true survivor bulb, shrugging off heat, humidity, and periods of both drought and standing water. Each summer stalk carries a dozen or more large, lightly fragrant, downward-nodding trumpets in soft pink with a darker pink midstripe down each petal. Leave the strappy foliage clump undisturbed for years, as flowering improves as the bulb cluster matures and offsets. Feed lightly in spring and mulch over winter in the cooler end of its range to protect the crown from hard freezes.

common_name: Emma Jones Crinum Lily (Fragrant Purplish-Pink Heirloom Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant the giant bulb with its shoulders at or just above soil level in rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, allowing several feet of clearance for the long arching leaves. This old Texas hybrid forms an especially large bulb and benefits from a deep planting hole amended with compost.

directions: Named by Texas bulb collector Thad Howard for a cross between the pass-along favorites 'Peachblow' and 'Cecil Houdyshel', this heirloom crinum carries glossy, three-foot strap leaves that cascade from a single massive bulb. Beginning in early summer, four-foot stalks open a dozen or more richly fragrant, purplish-pink trumpets that perfume the evening garden. It is still uncommon outside collector circles, so start with a large, blooming-size bulb and give it several seasons undisturbed before expecting a full flush of bloom. Water deeply during active summer growth, then let the soil dry between waterings once foliage begins to yellow in fall.

common_name: Bradley Crinum Lily (Compact Rosy-Pink Australian Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant bulbs with the neck near the soil surface in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to part shade. Its narrower, more upright foliage and compact clumping habit make it a good fit for large containers as well as in-ground beds.

directions: Bred from Crinum scabrum and Crinum flaccidum by the late Australian hybridizer H. B. Bradley, this dwarf crinum stays notably more compact than most garden hybrids while still sending up sturdy spikes of ten or more fragrant, deep rosy-pink flowers, each marked with a bright white eye. Its narrow, upright leaves form a tidy clump that offsets readily into a broad patch within a few seasons. The restrained size makes it an excellent choice for large patio containers or smaller borders where bigger crinums would overwhelm the space. Divide congested clumps in spring only when flowering begins to decline, since crinums generally bloom best when left undisturbed for years.
